SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Title:
Customer Clearing Documentation and Timing of Acceptance for Clearing (OMB Control No. 3038-0092). This is a request for an extension of a currently approved information collection.
Abstract:
Section 4d(c) of the Commodity Exchange Act (“CEA”), as amended by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (“Dodd-Frank Act”), directs the Commission to require futures commission merchants (“FCMs”) to implement conflict of interest procedures that address such issues as the Commission determines to be appropriate.
[
1
]
Similarly, section 4s(j)(5) of the CEA, as added by the Dodd-Frank Act, requires swap dealers (“SDs”) and major swap participants (“MSPs”) to implement conflict of interest procedures that address such issues as the Commission determines to be appropriate.
[
2
]
Section 4s(j)(5) also requires SDs and MSPs to ensure that any persons providing clearing activities or making determinations as to accepting clearing customers are separated by appropriate informational partitions from persons whose involvement in pricing, trading, or clearing activities might bias their judgment or contravene the core principle of open access. Section 4s(j)(6) of the CEA prohibits an SD or MSP from adopting any process or taking any
(
printed page 66693)
action that results in any unreasonable restraint on trade or imposes any material anticompetitive burden on trading or clearing, unless necessary or appropriate to achieve the purposes of the CEA.
[
3
]
Section 2(h)(1)(B)(ii) of the CEA requires that derivatives clearing organization (“DCO”) rules provide for the nondiscriminatory clearing of swaps executed bilaterally or through an unaffiliated designated contract market or swap execution facility.
[
4
]
To address these provisions, the Commission promulgated regulations that prohibit arrangements involving FCMs, SDs, MSPs, and DCOs that would (a) disclose to an FCM, SD, or MSP the identity of a customer's original executing counterparty;
[
5
]
(b) limit the number of counterparties with whom a customer may enter into a trade;
[
6
]
(c) restrict the size of the position a customer may take with any individual counterparty, apart from an overall credit limit for all positions held by the customer at the FCM;
[
7
]
(d) impair a customer's access to execution of a trade on terms that have a reasonable relationship to the best terms available;
[
8
]
or (e) prevent compliance with specified time frames for acceptance of trades into clearing set forth in Regulations 1.74(b), 23.610(b), or 39.12(b)(7).
[
9
]
Additionally, the Commission requires, through Regulation 39.12(b)(7)(i)(B), DCOs to coordinate with clearing members to establish prompt processing of trades.
[
10
]
Regulations 1.74(a) and 23.610(a) require reciprocal coordination by FCMs, SDs, and MSPs that are clearing members.
[
11
]
Under the above regulations, SDs, MSPs, FCMs, and DCOs are required to develop and maintain written customer clearing documentation and trade processing procedures. Maintenance of contracts, policies, and procedures is prudent business practice. All SDs, MSPs, FCMs, and DCOs maintain documentation consistent with these regulations. The regulations are crucial both for effective risk management and for the efficient operation of trading venues among SDs, MSPs, FCMs, and DCOs. Each of these entities has a general recordkeeping obligation for these requirements under the Regulations 39.20 for DCOs,
[
12
]
23.606 for SDs and MSPs,
[
13
]
and 1.73 for FCMs.
[
14
]
The information collection burden arising from the regulations primarily is restricted to the costs associated with the affected registrants' obligation to maintain records related to clearing documentation between the customer and the customer's clearing member, and trade processing procedures between DCOs and FCMs, SDs, and MSPs. The information collection obligations are necessary to implement certain provisions of the CEA, including ensuring that registrants exercise effective risk management, and are also appropriate for the efficient operation of trading venues among SDs, MSPs, FCMs, and DCOs.
As indicated below, the information collection burden arising from the regulations primarily is restricted to the costs associated with the affected registrants' obligation to maintain records related to clearing documentation between the customer and the customer's clearing member, and trade processing procedures between DCOs and FCMs, SDs, and MSPs. The information collection obligations are necessary to implement certain provisions of the CEA, including ensuring that registrants exercise effective risk management and for the efficient operation of trading venues among SDs, MSPs, FCMs, and DCOs.
An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number.
[
15
]
On August 6, 2026, the Commission published in the
Federal Register
notice of the proposed extension of this information collection and provided 60 days for public comment on the proposed extension,
91 FR 50814
(“60-Day Notice”). The Commission received no relevant comments on the 60-Day Notice.

As needed.
There are no capital costs or operating and maintenance costs associated with this collection.

et seq.
)

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Title:
Process for Review of Swaps for Mandatory Clearing (OMB Control No. 3038-0097). This is a request for extension of a currently approved information collection.
Abstract:
The Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations require a derivatives clearing organization (DCO) that wishes to accept a swap for clearing to be eligible to clear the swap and to submit the swap to the Commission for a determination as to whether the swap is required to be cleared. Commission Regulation 39.5 sets forth the process for these submissions. The Commission will use the information in this collection to determine whether a DCO that wishes to accept a swap for clearing is eligible to clear the swap and whether the swap should be required to be cleared. An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number.
On July 28, 2026, the Commission published in the
Federal Register
notice of the proposed extension of this information collection and provided 60 days for public comment on the proposed extension,
91 FR 47225
(“60-Day Notice”). The Commission received one comment from an anonymous submitter regarding its PRA burden estimates.
[
1
]
The comment asked how the Commission modeled or concluded that each registered DCO will submit one swap submission per year at an estimated 40 hours per submission.
The Commission's estimate of one submission per DCO per year is intended to account for variations in the number of swap submissions received by year by DCO. Some DCOs may be required to file multiple swap submissions in connection with the launch of new clearing initiatives, while other DCOs may not file any swap submissions in a given year.
The Commission's estimate of 40 hours per DCO submission is based on the Commission's experience reviewing the submissions. It considers the scope of topics the submissions must address, the level of detail typically provided by DCOs, the Commission's possible engagement with DCOs regarding submissions, and the nature of the information that may be sought by Commission staff. Generally, DCOs also have aggregated and presented information about new cleared swaps in other contexts, such as public marketing materials or as part of ongoing DCO supervision.
The comment also sought the Commission's rationale for its estimate that the regulation does not entail separate operation and maintenance costs for DCOs. The regulation requires only the provision of certain swap information that is part of other rule submissions done in the ordinary course of launching new cleared swap offerings. DCOs typically comply with this regulation along with other required Commission reporting and notifications.

On occasion. A DCO is only required to make a one-time submission before it first accepts a swap for clearing.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106696; File No. SR-CBOE-2026-081]
October 19, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 9, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) proposes to amend (i) Rule 5.33(g) to allow a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class to Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the
(
printed page 66745)
Complex Order Book (“COB”), where the Exchange has designated those groups as a related group and (ii) Rule 5.34 to allow for the Exchange (and Users, when applicable) to set risk control parameters on a related group basis when the Exchange is permitted to set parameters on a group basis. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​options/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​cone/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 5.33, which governs the trading of complex orders. The proposed additions to Rule 5.33(g)(6) would establish a related group framework under which a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class may Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the COB, if the Exchange has designated those groups as a related group and the other applicable legging restrictions that are currently enumerated under Rule 5.33 are satisfied.
Additionally, the Exchange also proposes to add interpretative guidance under Rule 5.34 to establish that, when the Exchange sets parameters for risk controls on a group basis, that the Exchange (or Users, when applicable) may also set parameters for a related group.
Background
Currently, the Exchange has authority under Rule 4.13(f) to list SPX or VIX on a group basis.
[
3
]
The Exchange currently lists SPX on a group basis; specifically, the Exchange lists A.M.-settled SPX options under the symbol SPX and lists P.M.-settled SPX options under the symbol SPXW. While SPX and SPXW options are part of the same S&P 500 Index options class, the Exchange may apply different trading parameters to SPXW options than those it applies to SPX options (pursuant to Rule 1.5).
[
4
]
SPX options reside on one matching engine while SPXW is on a separate matching engine. The Exchange intends to launch Weekly A.M.-settled SPX options (“SPXO”)
[
5
]
and list SPXO options as a separate group from both SPX and SPXW. However, SPXO and SPX options will both be on the same matching engine.
Legging
Under Rule 5.33(g) (“Legging”), a complex order may execute against orders and quotes resting in the Simple Book (pursuant to subparagraphs (d)(5)(A) and (e)) if it can execute in full or in a permissible ratio and has no more than the maximum number of legs, as the Exchange determines on a class-by-class basis, and is subject to a list of restrictions. Specifically, one such restriction under Rule 5.33(g)(6) states that “[i]f the Exchange determines to list SPX or VIX on a group basis pursuant to Rule 4.13, a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class may not Leg into the Simple Book. A complex order consisting of legs in the same group of series may Leg, subject to the other restrictions in this paragraph (g).” Pursuant to this provision, a complex order that consists of SPX and SPXW option legs is currently unable to leg into each underlying leg's Simple Book. The primary reason for this provision is because the Simple Books for SPX and SPXW are on different matching engines, as noted above.
However, SPXO options will be on the same matching engine as SPX options. As a result, Exchange technology will allow complex orders comprised of legs from these two different groups (SPXO and SPX) to leg into their respective Simple Books.
[
6
]
Complex orders that include an SPX or SPXO leg and an SPXW leg will continue to not be able to leg into their respective Simple Books.
In order to account for this, the Exchange proposes to add the related group framework to Rule 5.33(g)(6) so that a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series in the class that Cboe has designated as related groups may Leg into the Simple Book, in addition to being posted to the COB. The proposed related group framework reflects the current technological limitations of the Exchange's system. The Exchange will announce groups designated as related groups via Exchange Notice. The proposed change does not alter the existing Legging restrictions in Rule 5.33(g); rather, it adds a framework under proposed paragraph (g)(6) for the Exchange to designate groups as related, and thus permit complex orders comprised of legs from different groups to leg into their respective Simple Books, if Exchange technology can accommodate legging of complex orders comprised of legs for different groups. Because the Exchange remains unable to leg complex orders comprised of legs for groups that reside on different matching engines, only groups whose relevant series are processed by the same matching engine may be eligible for designation as a related group.
Risk Controls
Currently, Rule 1.5(c) grants the Exchange authority to set trading parameters on a group basis if parameters are set on a class-by-class basis and the Exchange determines to list SPX or VIX on a group basis pursuant to Rule 4.13. Rule 5.34 allows the Exchange to set several limits on a class by class basis.
[
7
]
Under current Rule 1.5, the Exchange has authority to set those parameters on a group basis when SPX or VIX is listed on a group basis.
The Exchange proposes to add interpretive guidance to allow for the Exchange (or Users, when applicable) to determine trading parameters under Rule 5.34 on a related group basis or on a group basis. The Exchange may designate groups as related for technological reasons, such as if they reside on the same matching engine. The Exchange will announce groups designated as related groups via Exchange Notice. Using SPX and SPXW
(
printed page 66746)
as an example, the Exchange looks at these as independent groups as they are on different matching engines (as described above) and because they are on different matching engines, the different risk checks enumerated under Rule 5.34 are applied to each group independently of each other.
[
8
]
However, currently, if groups reside on the same matching engine, such as SPX and SPXO will, the Exchange will designate them as a related group because the Exchange technology does not permit separate settings for different groups on the same matching engine. If the Exchange or User determines parameters on a related group basis, the products designated within a related group will be aggregated for the purpose of Rule 5.34.
For example, under Rule 5.34(c)(4)(A), the Exchange allows for class limits to be set on EFIDs for the notional contract volume. Under the proposed interpretation (and existing Rule 1.5), the Exchange may set these on a group-by-group basis. This would mean that SPX and SPXO would have their own independent limits (similar to the current practice for SPX and SPXW). However, under the proposed language, the Exchange also would have the ability to designate SPX and SPXO as a related group and then aggregate the volumes for SPX and SPXO together for the purpose of reviewing a specific risk check. Consider the following: a limit of $1,000,000 of notional contract volume for SPX is set for User A, this means, that User A's notional contract volume for both SPX and SPXO cannot exceed $1,000,000.
Lastly, when the Rules under 5.34 allow Users to set limits, they may also do so on a related group basis when applicable. For example, Rule 5.34(b)(6) permits Users to establish a higher or lower amount than the Exchange default buffer amount for a complex order to buy (sell) that is above (below) the SNBO (SNBB). Users may set this on a group basis, or under the proposed interpretative guidance, may also do so on a related group basis. When the Exchange sets limits on a related group basis, Users may also adjust these same related group limits.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”) and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
9
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
10
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
11
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
In particular, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change will remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, protect investors and the public interest, because allowing a complex order consisting of legs in different groups of series to Leg into the Simple Book when the Exchange has designated those groups as a related group will provide complex orders comprised of legs in groups that are related with greater opportunity to execute and contributes additional liquidity to the Simple Books, to the benefit of all market participants that interact with those books. While the Exchange may determine to list series of a class as groups to accommodate the different characteristics of those series, the Exchange believes it will benefit investors if it can technologically accommodate the legging of complex orders comprised of legs of those different groups to improve the likelihood of execution.
Additionally, by permitting the Exchange (and Users, when applicable) to determine parameters for a related group (and to aggregate volumes across a related group for the purpose of applicable risk checks) the proposed rule change protects investors by clarifying that the Exchange will link related groups for the purpose of risk checks due to technology reasons. Users, as needed, may adjust their risk settings accordingly to account for the aggregation of groups designated as a related group (
e.g.,
a firm may increase their limit if they plan to trade both products).
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is not designed to permit unfair discrimination because the enhanced Legging opportunity will be available to all complex orders consisting of legs in groups that the Exchange designates as a related group. Similarly, the interpretive guidance that the Exchange (and Users, when applicable) may determine parameters for a related group, applies uniformly to all market participants. The proposed rule change does not otherwise alter the restrictions applicable to Legging under Rule 5.33(g) or the risk controls under Rule 5.34.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because the proposed rule change will apply to market participants in the same manner.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because the proposed rule change concerns the operation of the Exchange's own legging functionality and risk controls. To the extent the proposed rule change makes the Exchange a more attractive marketplace, market participants on other exchanges are welcome to become Trading Permit Holders.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public
(
printed page 66747)
interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
12
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
13
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CBOE-2026-081 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CBOE-2026-081. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CBOE-2026-081 and should be submitted on or before November 12, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
14
]
Vanessa A. Countryman,
Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106695; File No. SR-LTSE-2026-23]
October 19, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 5, 2026, Long-Term Stock Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “LTSE”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing with the Commission a proposed rule change to adopt Supplementary Material .02 to Rule 14.210 (Dually-Listed Securities) to specify that all companies listing securities on LTSE must be listed on another registered national securities exchange (“Supplementary Material .02”).
The text of the proposed rule change is available at the Exchange's website at
https://longtermstockexchange.com/​
,
at the principal office of the Exchange and on the Commission's website at
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The self-regulatory organization has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to adopt Supplementary Material .02 to Rule 14.210 (Dually-Listed Securities) to specify that all companies listing securities on LTSE must be listed on another registered national securities exchange (“Supplementary Material .02”).
While LTSE maintains primary listing standards in its Rulebook and intends to operate as a primary listing market in the future, LTSE currently lists only issuers that also maintain a primary listing on another national securities exchange. The proposed rule text does not modify or eliminate LTSE's underlying initial or continued listing standards; instead, it clarifies the relationship between those standards and LTSE's current listing model for dually listed issuers.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6 of the Act,
[
5
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
6
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change promotes just and equitable principles of trade and protects investors by providing clear and transparent rules regarding LTSE's current listing model. Although LTSE maintains comprehensive primary listing standards within its Rulebook, LTSE currently operates under a model where listed issuers maintain a dual listing on another registered national securities exchange. The Exchange believes that codifying this requirement in proposed Supplementary Material .02 ensures that issuers, investors, and market participants have clarity regarding the requisite dual-listing status for LTSE-listed securities. By eliminating potential ambiguity surrounding LTSE's current listing operations, the proposed rule change prevents confusion in the marketplace and ensures that all market participants operate with a shared, precise understanding of LTSE's dual-listing framework.
Importantly, the proposed rule text does not modify, relax, or eliminate LTSE's existing initial or continued listing standards.
[
7
]
Instead, it simply clarifies the practical application of those standards in relation to LTSE's present operating model. By preserving underlying quality and governance benchmarks while harmonizing rule text
(
printed page 66757)
with operational reality, the Exchange maintains high listing standards that promote market integrity without disrupting existing trading mechanisms or regulatory oversight across the national market system.
The mandatory dual-listing requirement under Supplementary Material .02 will apply uniformly to all issuers listing securities on LTSE. Furthermore, the proposed rule change is identical in substance to existing rules previously approved or adopted by other self-regulatory organizations. Specifically, the proposed rule text mirrors Nasdaq Texas, LLC (“Nasdaq TX”) IM-5220-1, which similarly requires all companies listing on that exchange to maintain a dual-listing on another national securities exchange.
[
8
]
Adopting an identical approach establishes regulatory consistency across listing venues.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change fosters intermarket competition by clarifying the parameters under which issuers may list on LTSE while maintaining their primary listings elsewhere. Because the rule is substantively identical to Nasdaq Texas IM-5220-1, it ensures a level playing field among national securities exchanges that operate dual-listing structures.
The proposed rule will apply equally to all issuers listing securities on LTSE. Because the proposed rule merely codifies current operational practice and explicitly preserves the Exchange's underlying listing standards, it imposes no unexpected burdens on issuers or market participants while fostering fair and open competition within the national market system.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
9
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
10
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
11
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
12
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
13
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii),
[
14
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposal may become operative upon filing. The Exchange states that the proposed rule is identical to the rule of another national securities exchange.
[
15
]
Further, the Exchange states that the proposed change would add clarity and transparency to LTSE's Rulebook regarding its current listing model. For these reasons, and because the proposed rule change does not raise any new or novel regulatory issues, the Commission finds that waiving the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change as operative upon filing.
[
16
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange is filing a proposal to make a non-substantive correction to Exchange Rule 1014, Imposition of Fines for Minor Rule Violations.

II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Exchange Rule 1014(d)(5) to make a non-substantive correction to the table which describes violations of Rule 520(b). Specifically, the column titled, “Number of Violations Within One Calendar Year,” provides a numerical range of violations which corresponds to the second column which provides the associated sanction. For example, the first row provides that 1 to 5 violations will result in a sanction consisting of a Letter of Caution. Similarly, the second row provides that 6 to 10 violations within one calendar year will result in a sanction consisting of a fine in the amount of $500. The Exchange now proposes to correct the fourth row in the first column to state “16 to 20” whereas it currently incorrectly states “16 or 20.” The Exchange believes this correction will provide clarity and precision in the Exchange's rules and eliminate the potential for confusion regarding violations of Exchange Rule 520(b).
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act
[
3
]
in general, and further the objectives of Section 6(b)(1) of the Act
[
4
]
in particular, in that they are designed to enforce compliance by the Exchange's Members
[
5

and persons associated with its Members, with the provisions of the rules of the Exchange. In particular, the Exchange believes that the proposed change will provide greater clarity to Members and the public regarding the Exchange's Rulebook by making a non-substantive correction to rule text. The proposed change will also make it easier for Members to interpret the Exchange's Rulebook.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change also furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act. In particular, it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, promote just and equitable principles of trade, foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged
(
printed page 66767)
in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, remove impediments to and perfect the mechanisms of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange believes the proposed change promotes just and equitable principles of trade and remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system because the proposed rule change will provide greater clarity to Members and the public regarding the Exchange's Rulebook by making a non-substantive correction to rule text. It is in the public interest for the Exchange's Rulebook to be accurate and concise so as to eliminate the potential for confusion.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed change will not impose any burden on intra-market competition as there is no functional change to the Exchange's System
[
6
]
and because the rules of the Exchange apply to all Members equally. The proposed rule change will have no impact on competition as it is not designed to address any competitive issue but rather is designed to remedy a non-substantive issue and provide added clarity and precision to the Exchange's Rulebook. In addition, the Exchange does not believe the proposal will impose any burden on inter-market competition as the proposal does not address any competitive issues and is intended to protect investors by providing further clarity and accuracy regarding the Exchange's Rulebook.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
Written comments were neither solicited nor received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days after the date of the filing, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act

), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.3 (Criteria for Underlying Securities) and Rule 19.4 (Withdrawal of Approval of Underlying Securities) to (i) establish listing criteria and continued listing standards for options on shares of commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets, (ii) update Rule 19.3(i)(1) to permit the listing of options on an exchange traded fund as defined in Rule 6c-11 under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (“Rule 6c-11”),
[
5
]
and (iii) make conforming amendments to remove individual product-specific references and update cross-references within the rules.
Background
The Exchange's existing rules permit the listing and trading of options on various types of exchange-traded products, including options on shares of exchange-traded funds (“ETFs”), commodity pool ETFs, currency trust shares, and commodity-based trusts
(
printed page 66753)
holding a single crypto asset. Specifically, Rule 19.3(i) sets forth the criteria for securities deemed appropriate for options trading, including Fund Shares that are principally traded on a national securities exchange and defined as an “NMS stock” under Rule 600 of Regulation NMS.
Cboe Options Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe Options”), an affiliate of the Exchange, recently received approval from the Commission to list and trade options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets.
[
6
]
Specifically, Cboe Options adopted Rules 4.3.06(a)(6) and 4.4.06(c) to establish initial and continued generic listing criteria for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets.
[
7
]
Additionally, Cboe Options amended Rule 4.3.06(a)(4) to remove individual product-specific references for crypto asset ETPs, and in a separate filing
[
8
]
amended Rule 4.3.06(a)(1) to permit the listing of options on ETFs as defined in Rule 6c-11.
Proposed Rule Changes
The Exchange now proposes to adopt rules that are substantively identical to the Cboe Options Rules described above. Specifically, the Exchange proposes the following amendments.
Amendments to Rule 19.3(i)
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.3(i) to establish generic listing criteria for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets. Currently, Rule 19.3(i)(5) permits the listing of options on commodity-based trusts that hold a single crypto asset meeting certain requirements. The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.3(i)(5) to also permit the listing of options on commodity-based trusts that hold multiple crypto assets, provided that each underlying crypto asset held by such trust satisfies the following requirements:
i. the total global supply of each underlying crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust has an average daily market value of at least $700 million over the last 12 months; and
ii. each crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust underlies a derivatives contract that trades on a market with which the Exchange has a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement, whether directly or through common membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group (“ISG”).
These requirements are designed to ensure that each crypto asset underlying options approved for trading on the Exchange has sufficient market capitalization and is subject to adequate market surveillance. These criteria are substantively identical to those approved by the Commission for Cboe Options.
[
9
]
In addition, the Exchange proposes to update Rule 19.3(i)(1) to permit the listing of options on exchange traded funds as defined in Rule 6c-11, portfolio depositary receipts, or index fund shares. Proposed Rule 19.3(i)(1) is substantively identical to Cboe Rule 4.3.06(a)(1). The requirements of Rule 19.3(i)(1) are generally based on the generic listing standards for exchange-traded funds that pre-dated the adoption of Rule 6c-11. The Exchange proposes to eliminate the language from the rule text that specifies the securities and/or financial instruments that the entity holds and instead provide that the securities deemed appropriate for options trading shall include shares or other securities (“Fund Shares”), including but not limited to Partnership Units as defined in this Rule, that are principally traded on a national securities exchange and are defined as an “NMS stock” under Rule 600 of Regulation NMS, and that are listed pursuant to generic listing standards for an exchange-traded fund as defined in Rule 6c-11, portfolio depositary receipts, or index fund shares.
In 2019, the Commission adopted Rule 6c-11 to permit exchange-traded funds that satisfy certain conditions to operate without obtaining an exemptive order from the Commission under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
[
10
]
In 2020, the Commission approved generic listing standards pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) of the Exchange Act for exchange-traded funds that meet the requirements of Rule 6c-11 (
i.e.,
ETF Shares).
[
11
]
The Commission found that the ETF Shares generic listing standards are reasonably designed to help prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices particularly because a central qualification for listing generically is ongoing compliance with Rule 6c-11, which requires, among other things, ETF Shares to prominently disclose the portfolio holdings that will form the basis for each calculation of net asset value per share. The Commission stated that it believes that such portfolio transparency should help prevent manipulation of the price of ETF Shares.
[
12
]
The Exchange believes this same transparency rationale supports the generic listing of options on ETF Shares by aligning the options generic listing standards with the ETF Shares generic listing standards. This proposal simply creates a streamlined pathway for listing options on qualifying ETF Shares that meet the enhanced transparency standards under Rule 6c-11.
The Exchange believes this proposed listing standard for options on ETF Shares is reasonable and will result in options that are not readily susceptible to manipulation in light of existing Rule 6c-11 transparency requirements and options listing requirements.
[
13
]
The Commission has determined that portfolio transparency is central to preventing manipulation of ETF Share prices and serves as the primary qualification for generic listing of ETF Shares.
[
14
]
Where ETF Shares have been deemed sufficiently transparent to warrant generic listing, the Exchange believes the manipulation risks for both the underlying shares and overlying options are adequately mitigated through this transparency framework as options manipulation is typically achieved through manipulation of the underlying security.
The Exchange also proposes conforming amendments to renumber certain subparagraphs and cross-references within Rule 19.3(i) and to remove references to specific crypto asset ETPs from Rule 19.3(i)(4) for products that are now captured by the
(
printed page 66754)
generic criteria in proposed Rule 19.3(i)(5). Currently, Rule 19.3(i)(4) lists by name certain crypto asset ETPs approved for options trading. Because the proposed generic criteria in Rule 19.3(i)(5) would permit the listing of options on any commodity-based trust holding crypto assets that meet the specified requirements, the individual product-specific references to crypto asset ETPs in Rule 19.3(i)(4) are no longer necessary and are proposed to be removed.
The Exchange also proposes to redesignate the existing Fund Share criteria and additional listing requirements currently set forth in Rule 19.3(i) as Rule 19.3(i)(6)(A) and (B) and Rule 19.3(i)(7), respectively, with conforming updates to the lettering and numbering of subparagraphs thereunder. Additionally, the Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.3(i)(7)(i) to add “ETF Shares” as an additional category of generic listing standards, consistent with Cboe Options Rule 4.3, Interpretation and Policy .06(c)(1) and the amendments to Rule 19.3(i)(1), and to remove the reference to “series of” portfolio depositary receipts and index fund shares to align with the updated terminology throughout Rule 19.3(i).
The Exchange also proposes to correct erroneous cross-references in Rule 19.4(g). Currently, Rule 19.4(g)(1) references “Rule 19.3(i)(4)(A)” and Rule 19.4(g)(2) references “Rule 19.3(i)(4)(B)”; however, no such subparagraphs currently exist in Rule 19.3(i). The Exchange proposes to correct these cross-references to reference Rule 19.3(i)(6)(A) and Rule 19.3(i)(6)(B), respectively, which correspond to the redesignated Fund Share listing criteria. Cboe Options Rule 4.3.06(a)(4) similarly does not include individual product-specific references for crypto asset ETPs, instead relying on the generic listing criteria in Rule 4.3.06(a)(6). The Exchange's proposed conforming amendments follow this same approach by reorganizing Rule 19.3(i) to incorporate the new generic listing criteria for commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets while updating existing cross-references to maintain internal consistency within the rule.
Amendments to Rule 19.4(g)
Consistent with the Approval Order and Cboe Options Rule 4.4, Interpretation and Policy .06(e), the Exchange proposes to amend Rule 19.4(g) to establish continued listing standards applicable to options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets. In the Approval Order, the Commission approved Cboe Options' adoption of continued listing standards for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets, finding that such standards are designed to ensure ongoing compliance with the listing criteria and appropriate market surveillance. Similarly, the Exchange proposes to add a new subparagraph (3) to Rule 19.4(g) providing that the Exchange shall consider the suspension of opening transactions in any series of options of the class covering Fund Shares approved pursuant to Rule 19.3(i)(5) if the criteria under Rule 19.3(i)(5)(B)(i) are no longer satisfied, as determined by the Exchange on a monthly basis, or the criteria in Rule 19.3(i)(5)(B)(ii) are no longer satisfied.
[
15
]
The Exchange also proposes conforming amendments to update cross-references within Rule 19.4(g) to reflect the redesignation of Rule 19.3(i) subparagraphs. As discussed above, Rule 19.4(g)(1) and Rule 19.4(g)(2) currently contain erroneous cross-references to Rule 19.3(i)(4)(A) and Rule 19.3(i)(4)(B), respectively, which would be corrected to reference Rule 19.3(i)(6)(A) and Rule 19.3(i)(6)(B). The Exchange also proposes to renumber existing subparagraphs (3) and (4) of Rule 19.4(g) as subparagraphs (4) and (5), respectively.
These continued listing standards are substantively identical to those set forth in Cboe Options Rule 4.4.06(c) and are designed to ensure appropriate ongoing monitoring of crypto asset-based products listed on the Exchange.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
16
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
17
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
18
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act for the following reasons. First, with respect to the proposed initial and continued listing criteria for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets, the proposed amendments would permit the Exchange to list and trade such options using generic listing standards that are substantively identical to those set forth in Cboe Options Rules 4.3.06(a)(6) and 4.4.06(c). The requirements that each underlying crypto asset has an average daily market value of at least $700 million over the last 12 months and that each crypto asset underly a derivatives contract trading on a market with which the Exchange has a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices and to protect investors and the public interest.
Second, with respect to the proposed amendments to Rule 19.3(i)(1) to permit the listing of options on an exchange traded fund as defined in Rule 6c-11, these amendments are consistent with the approach taken by Cboe Options in the Proposal to List Options on 6c-11 ETFs.
[
19
]
The Exchange believes these amendments are consistent with the Act because existing Rule 6c-11 transparency requirements and options listing requirements are reasonably designed to help ensure that such options are not readily susceptible to manipulation. Where ETF Shares have been deemed sufficiently transparent to warrant generic listing, the Exchange believes the manipulation risks for both the underlying shares and overlying options are adequately mitigated through this transparency framework. This proposal creates a streamlined pathway for listing options on qualifying ETF Shares that meet the enhanced transparency standards under Rule 6c-11.
Third, with respect to the proposed amendment to Rule 19.3(i)(7)(i) to add ETF Shares, this amendment is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it ensures that Fund Shares listed pursuant to the ETF Shares generic listing standards are subject to the same additional listing requirements applicable to other categories of generically listed Fund Shares, thereby providing consistent investor
(
printed page 66755)
protections across all categories of generically listed fund products.
Fourth, with respect to the proposed conforming amendments to remove individual product-specific references in Exchange Rule 19.3(i)(4), remove the reference to “series of” portfolio depositary receipts and index fund shares, and update cross-references, these amendments are consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because they are designed to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market by aligning the Exchange's rules with the approach in Cboe Options Rule 4.3.06(a)(4), thereby promoting consistency across Cboe-affiliated exchanges without altering the substantive protections afforded to investors.
Fifth, with respect to the proposed amendments to Rule 19.4(g) to establish continued listing standards for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets and to update cross-references, these amendments are consistent with the Approval Order and are designed to ensure ongoing compliance with the listing criteria and appropriate market surveillance.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed rule change removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market by enabling market participants to trade options on multi-crypto-asset trusts on the Exchange under the same terms and conditions approved for Cboe Options. The proposed rule change promotes fair and orderly markets and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers, as the same generic listing criteria would apply equally to all eligible products.
The Commission has already determined that substantially identical rules satisfy the requirements of the Act in approving the Approval Order. The proposed amendments are also consistent with the Commission's prior approval of the Proposal to List Options on 6c-11 ETFs and with Cboe Options Rules 4.3.06(a)(4) and 4.3.06(a)(6), which established the framework for generic listing criteria that the Exchange now proposes to adopt. The Exchange therefore believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change is designed to permit the Exchange to list and trade options on the same types of products that have been approved for trading on Cboe Options and to adopt the same modernized descriptions and conforming amendments approved by the Commission for Cboe Options. Rather than imposing a burden on competition, the proposed rule change is designed to enhance competition by enabling the Exchange to compete on a level playing field with Cboe Options in offering options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets, listing options on 6c-11 ETFs, and applying generic listing criteria instead of product-specific references.
The Exchange notes that the proposed rule change does not impose any burden on intramarket competition, as the generic listing criteria would apply equally to all eligible products and market participants. The proposed rule change also does not impose any burden on intermarket competition, as it merely permits the Exchange to list the same types of products already approved for trading on another exchange.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
20
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
21
]
thereunder. Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; or (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
22
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
23
]
thereunder.
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
24
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b4(f)(6)(iii),
[
25
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposed rule change may become operative immediately upon filing. The Exchange proposes to amend its rules to establish listing criteria and withdrawal standards for options on Commodity-Based Trusts that hold multiple crypto assets. This aspect of the proposal would amend the Exchange's rules to be substantively identical in relevant part to rules governing listing standards and withdrawal criteria for options on Commodity-Based Trusts that hold multiple crypto assets on another options exchange, as discussed herein.
[
26
]
The Exchange also proposes to amend its rules to permit the listing of options on Exchange-Traded Funds as defined in Rule 6c-11 in a manner substantively identical in relevant part to rules on another exchange, as discussed herein.
[
27
]
The non-substantive technical edits conform the Exchange rulebook given the proposed substantive changes and will add clarity to the Exchange rulebook. This proposal does not raise any novel legal or regulatory issues. For these reasons, the Commission finds that waiver of the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Therefore, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change to be operative upon filing.
[
28
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
(
printed page 66756)
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
. Please include file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-067 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-067. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.  All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGX-2026-067 and should be submitted on or before November 12, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
29
]
Vanessa A. Countryman,
Secretary.
